documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Rebooked from November. Four weeks left on INH/rifampin, DOT going fine, nurse now comes on weekdays and he self-administers weekends under video check. No cough, no sweats. Weight back up. Hands stiff, he's counting down to the next rheum step.
Still not smoking or drinking, about 19 months.
O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear today. No jaundice. Synovitis MCPs both hands.
A/P:
1. Pulmonary TB, continuation phase, doing well. LFTs/CBC today, copy to TB clinic.
2. RA - rheum plans rituximab after TB treatment ends in February.
3. Lung screening CT: will plan the next one for fall rather than now, he's had several chest films this year and the TB clinic will do an end-of-treatment film.
RTC 3 months.

reports.text:
CHEST, PA AND LATERAL
Indication: Completion of treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis.
Comparison: 08/09/2024.
Findings: Marked interval improvement of the bilateral upper-lobe opacities. Residual linear scarring in the right upper lobe with mild volume loss. The previously seen cavity is no longer evident. No new consolidation. No pleural effusion. Heart and mediastinum normal.
reports.conclusion: Marked improvement. Residual right upper lobe scarring, no cavity.

documents.title: TB program completion letter
documents.author: public health TB clinic
documents.body:
HEALTH DEPARTMENT TUBERCULOSIS PROGRAM
Completion of treatment
Client: Craig Roy, DOB 05/19/1970

Mr. Roy completed six months of therapy for pan-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis on 02/10/2025: two months of isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol followed by four months of isoniazid and rifampin, all by DOT, with pyridoxine. Culture converted to negative at two months. No hepatotoxicity.

End-of-treatment chest film 02/11/2025: marked improvement, residual right upper lobe scarring with mild volume loss, cavity resolved.

Isoniazid, rifampin and pyridoxine stopped. His case is closed with our program. Given his immunosuppression, he knows to seek care promptly for cough, fever, sweats or weight loss.

TB nurse case manager, county health department

medications.sig: 1000 mg IV on day 1 and day 15, repeated every 6 months (infusion center)

documents.title: Rheumatology letter: rituximab
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY PRACTICE
Re: Craig Roy, DOB 05/19/1970

Dear colleague,

With his TB treatment completed on 02/10, Mr. Roy started rituximab for seropositive erosive RA. Hepatitis B surface antigen 02/25/2025 negative. He received rituximab 1000 mg IV on 03/04/2025 and 03/18/2025 in our infusion suite with premedication; no infusion reactions.

We will repeat the two-infusion course every six months, next due September. He continues methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid and prednisone 5 mg daily.

Medications: methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily, prednisone 5 mg daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Sincerely,
Rheumatology

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING
Indication: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2023. Annual screen. Treated pulmonary tuberculosis 2024-2025.
Comparison: LDCT 10/17/2023.
Findings: Linear and band-like scarring in the right upper lobe with mild volume loss, consistent with post-inflammatory change at the site of treated tuberculosis. No cavity. No solid, part-solid or ground-glass nodule. No consolidation. No pleural effusion, thickening or plaques. Heart size normal. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2: benign appearance. Right upper lobe post-inflammatory scarring. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrived 06/03/2026 19:25, discharged 06/04/2026 01:10
Patient: Craig Roy, 56 M

HPI: Four days of productive cough, fevers with chills, shortness of breath and sharp right-sided chest pain on deep breaths. Has seropositive RA on rituximab infusions every six months plus methotrexate and prednisone. Treated pulmonary TB 2024-25. Former smoker, former heavy drinker, sober for three years. Long construction career with asbestos exposure.

Triage: T 38.5 C, HR 108, RR 24, BP 118/72, SpO2 93% RA.
Exam: ill-appearing but conversant. Diminished breath sounds and crackles at the right base. Heart tachycardic, regular. No edema.

Results: WBC 13.6 with 84% neutrophils. BMP unremarkable. Blood cultures x2 drawn. Sputum sent for Gram stain and culture.
CXR: new right lower lobe consolidation; old RUL scarring unchanged.

Assessment: right lower lobe community-acquired pneumonia in an immunosuppressed patient. Imaging pattern not suggestive of TB recurrence. Observed in the ED, tolerating oral intake and walking without distress.

Disposition: discharged home. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily for 10 days and azithromycin 500 mg today then 250 mg daily for 4 days. Hold methotrexate until the antibiotic course is complete. Continue prednisone. Return for worsening breathing, chest pain or persistent fever. See PCP within one week.
Allergies: NKDA.

Booked post-ED visit 6/11, ED records requested.

documents.title: Office Visit - Post ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the regional ED 6/3 for RLL pneumonia. ED record and culture addendum reviewed: sputum grew pneumococcus, pen-sensitive; blood cultures negative.

Day 8 of 10 on amox-clav; azithro finished. Last fever Saturday. Cough looser, less of it, sputum now pale. Right-sided chest pain gone. Short of breath only on the stairs. Eating. Has been holding MTX since the ED as told. Still on pred 5.

Exam: afebrile, sat 97% RA, vitals as charted. A few crackles R base, otherwise clear. No dullness. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
1. Pneumococcal pneumonia RLL, improving on amox-clav (azithro done). Finish course. Repeat CBC today. Repeat PA/lat CXR in 6-8 wks to make sure it has cleared, given his smoking history and lung history; order placed.
2. RA on rituximab q6mo/MTX/pred. Keep MTX on hold until antibiotics are finished, then restart at the usual dose; message me when done. Rheum next course due Sept - will let them know about the pneumonia.
3. PCV20 given 2023. No further pneumococcal vaccine indicated now.
RTC September, sooner if fevers return.
